hyps.why: Replacing none with a conv adds an entire learned path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing weaker op.
Replacing none with a conv adds an entire learned path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing weaker op.
Replacing none with a conv adds an entire learned path from the input, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on 2->3 removes the most useful op, costing more than deleting a weak op like pool or none-like skip.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the direct input edge loses learned features, a bigger drop than deleting a weaker op.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on 1->3 loses learned capacity, costing more than deleting a weaker op.
Replacing none with a pool adds a path to node 3, which is a gain compared with swapping out an existing useful op.
Downgrading 3x3 to 1x1 on 2->3 loses spatial receptive field, which is worse than switching from other ops to 1x1.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with pooling discards learned capacity, which is a bigger loss than replacing a weaker op.
If 0->1 is already none, node 1 carries no signal, so removing 1->3 costs almost nothing.
